events.title: Caesar defeats Pompey at Pharsalus
events.description: Julius Caesar's veterans routed Pompey's larger army in Thessaly. Pompey fled to Egypt, where he was murdered, and Caesar became master of the Roman world.
events.html: Julius Caesar's veterans routed Pompey's larger army in Thessaly. Pompey fled to Egypt, where he was murdered, and Caesar became master of the Roman world.

events.title: Goths destroy a Roman army and kill Emperor Valens at Adrianople
events.description: Gothic cavalry and infantry overwhelmed the Eastern Roman army near Adrianople in Thrace, killing Emperor Valens and much of his force. Rome was never again able to expel the Goths from its territory.
events.html: Gothic cavalry and infantry overwhelmed the Eastern Roman army near Adrianople in Thrace, killing Emperor Valens and much of his force. Rome was never again able to expel the Goths from its territory.

events.title: Construction begins on the bell tower of Pisa
events.description: Work started on the campanile of Pisa Cathedral. Soft ground made it lean by the time the third storey was built, and it became famous as the Leaning Tower of Pisa.
events.html: Work started on the campanile of Pisa Cathedral. Soft ground made it lean by the time the third storey was built, and it became famous as the Leaning Tower of Pisa.

events.title: Pope John XXII creates the Diocese of Quilon in India
events.description: Pope John XXII, the second of the Avignon popes, created a Latin diocese at Quilon, in present-day Kollam in southern India, and appointed the French-born Jordanus as its first bishop.
events.html: Pope John XXII, the second of the Avignon popes, created a Latin diocese at Quilon, in present-day Kollam in southern India, and appointed the French-born Jordanus as its first bishop.

events.title: Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar defeats imperial troops at Wittenweiher
events.description: Near the village of Wittenweiher, now part of Schwanau in Baden-Württemberg, an army under the Protestant general Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar defeated imperial troops in the Thirty Years' War. The village was destroyed in the battle.
events.html: Near the village of Wittenweiher, now part of Schwanau in Baden-Württemberg, an army under the Protestant general Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar defeated imperial troops in the Thirty Years' War. The village was destroyed in the battle.

events.title: US bomber drops an atomic bomb on Nagasaki
events.description: The plutonium bomb Fat Man exploded over Nagasaki, killing some 40,000 people at once and many more later. Six days later Japan announced its surrender.
events.html: The plutonium bomb Fat Man exploded over Nagasaki, killing some 40,000 people at once and many more later. Six days later Japan announced its surrender.

events.title: Manson Family members murder Sharon Tate and four others
events.description: Followers of Charles Manson killed actress Sharon Tate, who was heavily pregnant, and four others at her Los Angeles home. The murders horrified America and Manson became a byword for evil.
events.html: Followers of Charles Manson killed actress Sharon Tate, who was heavily pregnant, and four others at her Los Angeles home. The murders horrified America and Manson became a byword for evil.

events.title: Gerald Ford becomes president after Nixon resigns
events.description: Gerald Ford was sworn in as the 38th president, telling Americans 'our long national nightmare is over'. His pardon of Nixon a month later probably cost him the 1976 election.
events.html: Gerald Ford was sworn in as the 38th president, telling Americans 'our long national nightmare is over'. His pardon of Nixon a month later probably cost him the 1976 election.
